# Cluster options

<!-- GENERATED by tests/ArcaneCore.World.Tests/Docs (ConfigReferenceRenderer.RenderByArea) from the options classes. Do not edit by hand.
     Regenerate: ARCANECORE_UPDATE_DOCS=1 dotnet test tests/ArcaneCore.World.Tests --filter Docs -->

58 options. Set them in the daemon's `.conf` file or `appsettings.json`. Full reference: [configuration.md](../configuration.md). All areas: [index](README.md).

Daemon says which server reads it. Reload says whether `.reload config` applies it: `live` is applied to the running server, `restart` keeps its value until the next start, `start` is read once when the daemon starts.

## `Cluster:Fencing`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowSqliteWorkerScope` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | With Scope=Worker, allows a SQLite characters database. Off by default: a split cluster needs PostgreSQL or MariaDB; only in-process tests set it. |
| `ClaimWatchIntervalSeconds` | `int` | `10` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | With fencing disabled, how often the world reads the characters ownership row to notice that a fenced world has claimed the database, in seconds (1 to 300). Independent of autosave; an unfenced world can keep writing for up to this long after a claim. |
| `Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World, Gateway | start | Enable durable character ownership fencing at world startup; disabled by default. Mandatory in worker mode (Cluster:Worker:Enabled): a worker with fencing off refuses to start. Also required (startup check, exit 78) with Cluster:Node:Role other than Combined and for every world child of a Cluster:Supervisor that runs more than one world: an unfenced world skips the durable id allocator priming and collides on in-memory id counters. Each world of such a cluster needs its own OwnerNode and Cluster:Worker:NodeId, on a PostgreSQL or MariaDB characters database. The gateway reads this key too: with it or Cluster:Worker:Enabled true, the write fence is attached to the gateway's own characters connection (the handoff and transfer journals). |
| `HeartbeatSeconds` | `int` | `10` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | With Scope=Worker, how often the worker records that it is alive on its ownership row, in seconds (1 to 60). A reap only ever fires on a heartbeat older than ReapAfterSeconds. |
| `OwnerNode` | `string` | `"<machine-name>"` | text | World | start | The durable owner identity; defaults to the current machine name and must be stable while the world owns the database. Must be distinct for each world of a multi-world cluster (the supervisor check refuses a duplicate). |
| `ReapAfterSeconds` | `int` | `150` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | With Scope=Worker, the age of a worker row's last heartbeat before another worker may reap it as dead, in seconds (30 to 3600, and more than three heartbeats). Keep it above the advisory lock's stale-session timeout (about 4 x 30 s). |
| `ReapDeadOwners` | `bool` | `true` | true \| false | World | start | With Scope=Worker, whether a worker may reap a dead shard (lock free and heartbeat older than ReapAfterSeconds) so its characters become claimable; false leaves that to an operator. Ignored in Realm scope. |
| `Scope` | `CharacterFencingScope` | `Realm` | Realm \| Worker | World | start | Which durable ownership scope this world claims: Realm (the default, one realm-wide writer, exactly as before) or Worker (one scope per map worker shard, so several workers write the same characters database). Worker needs Cluster:Worker:Enabled, Cluster:Fencing:Enabled, Cluster:Node:Role=MapWorker, a non-empty explicit Cluster:Worker:OwnedMaps and a PostgreSQL or MariaDB characters database (SQLite only with AllowSqliteWorkerScope). Values: `Realm`, `Worker`. |
| `Shard` | `string` | `""` | text | World | start | With Scope=Worker, the shard id this worker claims and locks (1 to 57 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 : . _ -); empty uses Cluster:Worker:NodeId. A standby sets the active worker's shard so a handoff hands over the same scope. Shard ids must be unique per world child, ignoring case. |
| `TakeoverEpoch` | `long?` | `null` | a whole number, -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807 | World | start | The positive ownership epoch to compare and swap during an explicit takeover; pair with `TakeoverIncarnation`. |
| `TakeoverIncarnation` | `Guid?` | `null` | text | World | start | The non-empty ownership incarnation to compare and swap during an explicit takeover; pair with `TakeoverEpoch`. |

## `Cluster:Node`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AuthorityLeaseRenewSeconds` | `int` | `10` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | How often a held lease is renewed (1 to a third of the TTL). A node that cannot renew in time stops itself rather than run a singleton without the lease. Only used when Role is not Combined. |
| `AuthorityLeaseTtlSeconds` | `int` | `30` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | How long a realm singleton lease stays valid without a renewal (5 to 600). A node that dies releases its singletons to another node after this long. Only used when Role is not Combined. |
| `Role` | `ClusterNodeRole` | `Combined` | Combined \| Gateway \| MapWorker \| Social \| Economy | World | start | The role this World process runs as: `Combined` (the default) runs every feature here. `MapWorker` needs Cluster:Worker:Enabled = true; the realm-wide singletons (the auction house bot and AutoBroadcast) then run on this node only while it holds their database lease. `Social`, `Economy` and `Gateway` are refused on a World process: the shared auction, mail and presence state they would need does not exist yet. Values: `Combined`, `Gateway`, `MapWorker`, `Social`, `Economy`. |

## `Cluster:NodeBridge`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `true` starts the node bridge: the World connects to each endpoint in `Endpoints`, logs node connection events and heartbeats, and syncs live worker placement. `false`, the default, does nothing at all: no sockets, no log lines, no background task. Read once when the daemon starts. |
| `Endpoints` | `string` | `"worker:EK\|Worker\|127.0.0.1:19081\|0;worker:Kalimdor\|Worker\|127.0.0.1:19082\|1;worker:instances\|Worker\|127.0.0.1:19083\|30,33,34,35,36,43,47,48,70,90,109,129,189,209,229,230,249,289,309,329,349,369,389,409,429,449,450,469,489,509,529,531,533;gateway\|Gateway\|127.0.0.1:19084\|-;supervisor\|Supervisor\|127.0.0.1:19087\|-"` | text | World | start | The nodes the bridge monitors, as `;`-separated entries of `nodeId\|role\|host:port\|maps`, where `maps` is a comma list of map ids or `-` for a realm-wide node. The default is the five local nodes a split cluster runs: worker:EK 19081, worker:Kalimdor 19082, worker:instances 19083, gateway 19084, supervisor 19087. A blank value means the five default nodes; a launcher that starts other nodes sets this to exactly those. The ARCANECORE_CLUSTER_ENDPOINTS environment variable, when set, replaces it but does not turn the bridge on (a warning is logged when `Enabled` is false). Only read when `Enabled` is true. |

## `Cluster:Peer`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `BindAddress` | `string` | `"127.0.0.1"` | text | World | start | Address the lease holder listens on. Keep it on loopback or a private network: the link is not encrypted. |
| `Endpoints` | `List<PeerEndpointEntry>` | `[]` | a list: numbered keys 0, 1, 2, ...; each entry is a group of keys | World | start | List form of `Nodes` for node ids that contain `:` (for example `worker:EK`). Configuration keys use `:` as the section separator, so `Nodes:worker:EK` would nest instead of naming a key. Bind each entry as `Cluster:Peer:Endpoints:0:NodeId` and `Cluster:Peer:Endpoints:0:Address` (`host:port`). `ResolveNodes` merges both forms; an `Endpoints` entry wins over a `Nodes` entry with the same id, and a node id listed twice in `Endpoints` is invalid. |
| `HandshakeTimeoutMs` | `int` | `5000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | How long, in milliseconds, a new link may take to answer the challenge and say hello before it is closed. |
| `HolderPollMs` | `int` | `1000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | How often, in milliseconds, a client re-reads the lease store to notice that the holder changed (a link to a former holder is dropped and the new holder is dialled). |
| `MaxPendingRequests` | `int` | `256` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Most requests a client may have in flight; one more is refused at once instead of queued. |
| `Nodes` | `Dictionary<string, string>` | `{}` | a map: one key per entry name; each value is text | World | start | Where each node's peer listener is, by node id (`Cluster:Worker:NodeId`) to `host:port`. A node that finds the lease holder in the lease store looks its endpoint up here; a holder without an entry is not dialled. |
| `Port` | `int` | `8097` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Port the lease holder listens on (0 lets the operating system pick one, for tests). |
| `ReconnectInitialMs` | `int` | `250` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | First wait, in milliseconds, before a client redials a lost or refused link; it doubles per failed attempt up to `ReconnectMaxMs` and resets once a link is admitted. |
| `ReconnectMaxMs` | `int` | `10000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Longest wait, in milliseconds, between redials. |
| `RequestTimeoutMs` | `int` | `5000` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | How long, in milliseconds, a request waits for its answer before it fails with a timeout. |

## `Cluster:Supervisor`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ChildStateFile` | `string` | `"logs/supervisor-children.json"` | text | World | start | Where the supervisor records the children it owns (name, role, pid, start time; default `logs/supervisor-children.json`, relative to the working directory; empty turns the record off). A restarted supervisor reads it to adopt or terminate children a crashed predecessor left running. |
| `CrashLoopMaxRestarts` | `int` | `5` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | How many times a child may be restarted within `CrashLoopWindowSeconds` before the supervisor gives up on it (default 5; 1 to 1000): that many restarts are allowed, and the next failure inside the window (the one after the last allowed restart) leaves it Faulted and is recorded in the fault and anomaly ledgers. A restart request (exit code 2) after a healthy run does not count. |
| `CrashLoopWindowSeconds` | `int` | `300` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | The window the crash-loop count is taken over, in seconds (default 300; 10 to 86400). |
| `DumpGraceSeconds` | `int` | `420` | a whole number of seconds, 1 to 3600 | World | start | The cap on how long a child that announced `dumping` (its own crash dump, `Diagnostics:CrashDump`) is exempt from the hang timeout and from a hang capture of the supervisor's own, in seconds (default 420: three times the default dump timeout of 120 s, plus a minute; 1 to 3600). The exemption is `min(announced max + 60, this)`: the child's own `max=` from its authenticated line, bounded by this value. Keep it above three times the child's `Diagnostics:CrashDump:TimeoutSeconds` plus a minute, or the cap cuts a long dump short. |
| `Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | Runs this World process as the host supervisor only (default: false): it launches and watches the configured `Processes` and starts no world, database, listener or feature. Off, a World start is unchanged. |
| `HangCaptureDirectory` | `string` | `"logs/supervisor-captures"` | text | World | start | Where hang captures (stack reports and dumps) are written (default `logs/supervisor-captures`); relative to the working directory. |
| `HangCaptureTimeoutSeconds` | `int` | `300` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | The longest a hang capture may take before the supervisor drains and kills the child anyway, in seconds (default 300; 1 to 3600). |
| `HealthyUptimeSeconds` | `int` | `120` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | A child that ran this many seconds (default 120; 1 to 86400) before it exited is healthy: its restart backoff starts over at the minimum and an exit-code-2 restart is not a crash-loop failure. |
| `MaxConcurrentProcesses` | `int` | `9` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Maximum number of concurrent supervised child processes allowed on this host (default: 9). |
| `MaxTotalAllocatedMemoryMb` | `long?` | `null` | a whole number, -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807 | World | start | Optional cap on the sum of `SupervisedProcessConfig.RequiredMemoryMb` across all active supervised processes. |
| `MinClusterProcesses` | `int` | `3` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Minimum number of supervised processes a supervisor start must be able to admit (realm, gateway and one worker; default: 3). A start that can admit fewer launches nothing and refuses with a message naming this key. |
| `MinFreeMemoryReserveMb` | `long` | `1024` | a whole number, -9223372036854775808 to 9223372036854775807 | World | start | Minimum free host memory reserve in MiB that must remain after admitting a child process (default: 1024 MiB). |
| `Processes` | `Dictionary<string, SupervisedProcessConfig>` | `{}` | a map: one key per entry name; each entry is a group of keys | World | start | Supervised process definitions, started in ascending `SupervisedProcessConfig.StartOrder` (ties by key), keyed by a configuration key that must not contain `:` (e.g. `worker-EK`); the display name may, via `SupervisedProcessConfig.Name` (`worker:EK`). |
| `RestartDelayMs` | `int` | `0` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Milliseconds the supervisor waits before it relaunches a child that exited with the restart code 2 (default 0; 0 to 600000). Crashes use the backoff instead. |
| `StackCaptureTool` | `string` | `""` | text | World | start | The dotnet-stack executable for `HangCapture=Stacks` (default empty: none; required when any child uses Stacks). |
| `StartGroupReadySeconds` | `int` | `0` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Seconds the supervisor waits, before it launches the next `SupervisedProcessConfig.StartOrder` group, for every child of the group it just launched to send its first `alive` heartbeat (default 0: do not wait; 0 to 3600). A child that exits first, or a group still silent after this long, stops the wait with a warning and the start goes on. A split topology sets it so the schema-DDL holder is up before the validate-only worlds check the schema. Needs children that heartbeat to the supervisor (`Ops:Watchdog` on). |
| `StopWhenBelowMinimum` | `bool` | `true` | true \| false | World | start | Stop everything when fewer than `MinClusterProcesses` children are left running (default true): the rest are drained and the supervisor exits 0 when every stop was deliberate and 1 when a child was given up on. Off, the supervisor keeps the remaining children running. |

## `Cluster:Worker`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `AllowInstanceMaps` | `bool` | `true` | true \| false | World | start | With an OwnedMaps list: whether instance copies (dungeons, raids, battlegrounds) of maps outside the list also run on this worker. `true`, the default, lets a continent worker host the instances it hands out; `false` refuses them. Ignored while OwnedMaps is empty. |
| `BindAddress` | `string` | `"127.0.0.1"` | an IPv4 or IPv6 address such as 127.0.0.1 or ::1 (host names are not resolved) | World | start | Address of the gateway listener. Keep it on loopback or a private network: the link is not encrypted. |
| `CharactersSchemaVersion` | `int` | `75` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Characters schema version both ends must agree on (an override label, used only while `VersionsFromDatabase` is false). |
| `ContentRevision` | `string` | `"world-schema-69"` | text | World | start | Content revision label both ends of the link must agree on; an override, used only while `VersionsFromDatabase` is false. |
| `Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World, Gateway | start | `true` opens the gateway listener (worker mode) and makes character fencing mandatory: Cluster:Fencing:Enabled must be true, and the characters write fence is attached either way. `false`, the default, is Combined mode: no listener, no change. The gateway reads this key too, only to attach the write fence to its own characters connection (the handoff and transfer journals), as it does for Cluster:Fencing:Enabled. |
| `LinkSecret` | `string` | `""` | text | World | start | Shared secret a gateway proves (HMAC-SHA256 of a per-link challenge) before it may open sessions; must equal Gateway:LinkSecret. Required in worker mode on every bind address, loopback included: at least 16 characters, or the world refuses to start. An admitted gateway opens sessions for any account it authenticated, so treat the secret like a database password. |
| `NodeId` | `string` | `"world"` | text | World | start | This worker's node id in the link manifest (shown in the gateway's log). |
| `OwnedMaps` | `string` | `""` | text | World | start | The maps this worker owns, as a list of ids and inclusive ranges (`0,1,30-40`; separators comma, semicolon or space). Empty, the default, owns every map, which keeps the combined behaviour. With a list, the world never creates or enters a map outside it (login, teleport, spawn, bot travel refuse cleanly until redirects and far transfers to the owning worker exist), and the list is announced in the link manifest. Lists of different workers must not overlap (the supervisor's Processes:*:Maps check). |
| `Port` | `int` | `8095` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Port of the gateway listener; must equal the gateway's Gateway:WorkerPort. |
| `RealmId` | `int` | `1` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | Realm id both ends of the link must agree on. |
| `Standby` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | Standby (Tier 3b handoff target; needs Enabled): start the process, build its services and link to the gateway, but admit no session, claim no characters ownership, run no schema DDL, take no writer lock until promoted (promotion takes it and is refused while the old world holds it), open no World:Port listener, and attach no feature nor start the simulation until promoted by a handoff (features read the characters database, which the active world still owns). `false`, the default, is an active worker. |
| `VersionsFromDatabase` | `bool` | `true` | true \| false | World | start | `true`, the default, advertises the versions the databases record (characters and world schema version rows, and a content revision derived from the world schema version; an unreadable version refuses to link) instead of the three labels below, so a worker and gateway on mixed versions are refused at admission. The worker logs the values it advertises at start. `false` advertises the labels (the explicit override; tests and operators who pin them). The gateway has no database access: set its Gateway:* labels to the values the worker logs, or every gateway is refused. |
| `WorldSchemaVersion` | `int` | `69` | a whole number, -2147483648 to 2147483647 | World | start | World schema version both ends must agree on (an override label, used only while `VersionsFromDatabase` is false). |

## `Cluster:Worker:Handoff`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `true` lets an admitted gateway drive this worker's side of a whole-World handoff over the gateway link (Describe, Warm, StopAdmissions, Freeze, Flush, Resume, ReleaseWriterLock, Retire, Promote; needs Cluster:Worker:Enabled). `false`, the default, answers every handoff request Disabled. |

## `Cluster:Worker:Transfers`

| Option | Type | Default | Allowed | Daemon | Reload | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Enabled` | `bool` | `false` | true \| false | World | start | `true` builds this worker's production transfer source and target and lets an admitted gateway drive them over the gateway link (TargetDescribe, Reserve, Install, Activate, Discard, Suspend, ResumeSource, RetireSource; needs Cluster:Worker:Enabled). `false`, the default, answers every transfer request Disabled. |
